ei.subject: 영어1
ei.title: Endurance on the Endurance / Wounded Healer

fullPassage:
On August 1, 1914, Ernest Shackleton departed London on the ship Endurance with 27 men and 69 dogs to cross the Antarctic continent. Little did they know the journey ahead would be one of the most challenging adventures in history.
The crew members were full of excitement, but when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice on January 18, 1915, their joy quickly turned to fear. "Oh, my! It's frozen like an almond in the middle of a chocolate bar!" cried one of the crew members. Shackleton and his men had to abandon their ship and set up camp on the floating ice, where they would be forced to spend the winter. Each man was given a sleeping bag and was assigned to one of five tents. Shackleton yielded the better sleeping bags to other crew members and chose to stay with the group's more troublesome characters who could get involved in conflicts. The camping mats were not waterproof, so they were constantly wet. The men shivered in the severe cold and suffered from frostbite. Worst of all, the floating ice on which they were camped began cracking beneath them. Shackleton walked around inspecting the ice regularly for the crew members' safety. Some nights, Shackleton and his men had to pick up their tents, moving their camp to a more secure area where the ice was less likely to break.
Days went by, and all the crew members could see for miles around was ice. Despite the hopeless situation, Shackleton tried to make the crew at ease with his humor. A crew member even played his banjo to relieve the crew members' anxiety and depression. Seldom were they happy, though. In the rare happy moments, music became a kind of mental medicine. Shackleton's open and honest communication was helpful to the crew members.
The crew members struggled in the hope of getting back on the Endurance one day, but that day would never come. "She's going, boys!" Shackleton shouted on the evening of November 21, 1915, witnessing his ship finally breaking up and sinking into the Weddell Sea.
The 28 men were now isolated on drifting ice hundreds of miles from land, with no ship, no means of communication with the outside world, and limited supplies. Realizing the need for a new survival plan, Shackleton established daily routines for his men. The crew members began each day with breakfast and performed daily tasks such as hunting for food and making improvements to the three lifeboats which were previously rescued from the sunken ship. Time was also set aside for activities like reading or exercising. The crew sang songs, celebrated their crew members' birthdays, and even played football matches on the ice. Even in these occasional moments of joy, at night, the men had to take turns watching for any ice breaking beneath their feet.
On April 9, 1916, the floating ice began to crack, and Shackleton gave the order: "Launch the boats." They traveled across the sea ice and then the open water. They fought against freezing sea water pouring into the boats before they finally reached Elephant Island 6 days later, on April 15. The island was far from any shipping routes, so they were not likely to be found and rescued.
On April 20, with four crew members, Shackleton set off on a risky journey in a small lifeboat to seek help from a whaling station on South Georgia Island, which was 1,300 km away. He took some of the troublesome characters with him so that the remaining crew would not fight while on Elephant Island. Each morning on the island, Frank Wild, whom Shackleton had left in charge, called everyone to be ready to depart. "The Boss may come today!" he declared daily.
Shackleton and the four crew members finally reached South Georgia Island on May 10. Still, their struggle was not over yet. The whaling station was located on the other side of a mountain range. They had to cross the rocky mountains on foot. They stopped to rest for a while, and the exhausted men fell asleep right away. Shackleton woke them up after only a five-minute nap, which saved them from freezing to death. When they arrived at the whaling station, Shackleton hurried to arrange for a rescue ship, the Yelcho, to be sent to Elephant Island.
On August 30, 1916, the crew members on Elephant Island spotted a ship. Upon hearing the news of the rescue ship's arrival, everyone rushed out of camp. "Are you alright?" Shackleton called out. "All well!" came the reply. All 28 men on the island were rescued alive and safe. After 634 days of drifting in the Antarctic, the crew had finally reached the end of their long and harsh journey.
"I have done it," Shackleton wrote to his wife. "Not a life lost, and we have been through hell."
A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is credited with coining the term "a wounded healer." He stated that "We don't get wounded alone, and we don't heal alone." Then what does "a wounded healer" mean? Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to help others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer. People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who overcome suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can evolve into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership would be transformative because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills. Leaders who have dealt with their wounds find themselves more at peace. Therefore, their leadership style is characterized by the ability to embrace the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing: accepting different perspectives and focusing on personal development while pursuing their goals.

questions.passage: On August 1, 1914, Ernest Shackleton departed London on the ship Endurance with 27 men and 69 dogs to cross the Antarctic continent. Little did they ①<u>know</u> the journey ahead would be one of the most challenging adventures in history. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ②exciting→excitement: 전치사 of 뒤에는 명사가 와야 함.
det.analysis:
✅ ② exciting → excitement: 'full of' 뒤에는 명사가 필요. exciting은 형용사.
❌ ① know: Little did they know 도치 구문 올바름
❌ ③ turned: joy turned to fear 올바름
❌ ④ forced: would be forced 수동태 올바름
det.tip: be full of + 명사: excitement(명사) vs exciting(형용사)

questions.passage: The 28 men were now isolated on drifting ice hundreds of miles from land. Realizing the need for a new survival plan, Shackleton ①<u>establishing</u> daily routines for his men. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①establishing→established: 주절 동사가 필요한데 현재분사형이 쓰임.
det.analysis:
✅ ① establishing → established: 분사구문(Realizing...) 뒤 주절에는 동사 원형 필요.
❌ ② performed: 과거시제 올바름
❌ ③ which: 관계대명사 올바름
❌ ④ like: 전치사 '~와 같은' 올바름
det.tip: 분사구문 + 주절(주어+동사). 주절에 또 분사를 쓰면 동사 부재.

questions.passage: On April 20, with four crew members, Shackleton set off on a risky journey in a small lifeboat to seek help from a whaling station on South Georgia Island, ①<u>which</u> was 1,300 km away. He took some of the troublesome characters with him so that the remaining crew would not fight ②<u>while</u> on Elephant Island. Each morning on the island, Frank Wild, ③<u>whom</u> Shackleton had left in charge, called everyone to be ready to depart. "The Boss may come today!" he ④<u>declaring</u> daily.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④declaring→declared: 주어 he의 서술어 동사가 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ declaring → declared: 과거 시제 동사 필요.
❌ ① which: 관계대명사, 선행사 South Georgia Island
❌ ② while: 접속사 올바름
❌ ③ whom: 목적격 관계대명사 올바름
det.tip: whom: Shackleton had left (whom) in charge에서 left의 목적어

questions.passage: Days went by, and all the crew members could see for miles around ①<u>was</u> ice. Despite the hopeless situation, Shackleton tried to make the crew at ease with his humor. det.analysis:

❌ ① was: all ~ could see was ice 올바름
❌ ③ helpful: be helpful to 올바름
❌ ④ getting: in the hope of ~ing 올바름

det.korean: 한 대원은 대원들의 불안감과 우울함을 덜어주기(relieve) 위해 밴조를 연주했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ relieve: 덜어주다 — 불안감을 완화하는 맥락
❌ ① intensify: 강화하다 — 반의어
❌ ② aggravate: 악화시키다 — 반의어
❌ ④ ignore: 무시하다 — 맥락 부적합
det.tip: relieve(덜어주다) ↔ intensify/aggravate(강화/악화시키다)

questions.passage: Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences ①<u>enable</u> them to help others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' hardships. People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who ②<u>surrender to</u> suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can ③<u>evolve</u> into "wounded leaders." questions.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ②surrender to(굴복하다)→overcome(극복하다): 고통을 '극복하는' 사람들이 치유자가 됨.
det.analysis:
✅ ② surrender to 부적절 → 원문 overcome. 치유자가 되려면 굴복이 아닌 극복.
❌ ① enable: 원문 그대로
❌ ③ evolve: 원문 그대로
❌ ④ understand: 원문 그대로
det.tip: overcome(극복하다) ↔ surrender to(굴복하다)

questions.passage: On August 1, 1914, Ernest Shackleton departed London on the ship Endurance with 27 men and 69 dogs to cross the Antarctic continent. The crew members were full of excitement, but when their ship got stuck in thick pack ice on January 18, 1915, their joy quickly turned to fear.
questions.stem: Shackleton은 1914년에 남극 대륙 횡단을 위해 출발했으나, 1915년 1월에 배가 런던으로 돌아왔다.

det.korean: 배가 총빙에 갇혔지(got stuck) 돌아오지(returned) 않았다. False.
det.analysis: F: 'got stuck in thick pack ice' ≠ returned to London.
det.tip: got stuck(갇히다) ≠ returned(돌아오다)

questions.passage: Shackleton yielded the better sleeping bags to other crew members and chose to stay with the group's more troublesome characters who could get involved in conflicts. The camping mats were not waterproof, so they were constantly wet.

det.korean: 원문 그대로. True.
det.analysis: T: yielded better sleeping bags + chose to stay with troublesome characters.
det.tip: yield: 양보하다. troublesome characters: 골칫거리 인물

questions.passage: Shackleton and the four crew members finally reached South Georgia Island on May 10. Still, their struggle was not over yet. The whaling station was located on the other side of a mountain range. They had to cross the rocky mountains on foot.

det.korean: 포경 기지는 산맥 반대편이라 걸어서 넘어야 했다. False.
det.analysis: F: 'struggle was not over yet' + 'other side of a mountain range'.
det.tip: 세부 변조: '도착하자마자' ≠ 원문 (산을 넘어야 했음)

❌ ④ 타고난 능력: 상처 경험이 키운다고 함
det.tip: 핵심: 고통 경험 + 극복 = 치유자 → 리더

questions.passage: Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to help others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer. People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who overcome suffering who can become wounded healers.
questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 영어를 위 글의 내용을 바탕으로 쓰시오.

"Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to __________."

det.korean: 상처 입은 치유자는 고통스러운 경험을 통해 다른 사람들을 도울 수 있는(help others) 사람이다.
det.analysis:
원문: 'painful experiences enable them to help others'
빈칸: help others
det.tip: enable + 목적어 + to V: ~가 ...하는 것을 가능하게 하다
